subject: Post-demo: pilot pricing, monthly spend band & PO thresholds (Orbital Commerce)
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@orbitalcommerce.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Mar 2027 14:04:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: pilot pricing, monthly spend band & PO thresholds (Orbital Commerce)

Thanks again for the demo time earlier — good conversation. Quick summary and a couple of asks so we can move to procurement: 

- Recap: Orbital is evaluating Redwood for real-time recommendations + personalization (inference for ranking and short-form generation).
- Ask 1: Can you confirm a target monthly token range for the pilot (rough ballpark is fine — e.g., 1–5M, 5–15M, 15–50M tokens/month)?
- Ask 2: Procurement rules: what is the minimum PO or contract value they need to issue for net-30 terms (if any)?

To make budgeting easier I attached a one-page pricing sheet. High-level unit economics we typically use for pilots/early production (these are starting points and can be refined with a committed band):

- Pilot / Pay-as-you-go: $2,400 per 1M tokens (no commit) — good for ad-hoc testing
- Small committed band (>=10M tokens/month): $1,600 per 1M tokens
- Mid committed band (>=30M tokens/month): $1,000 per 1M tokens

Example math (simple): if you estimate 10M tokens/month and we price at $1,600/1M -> ~ $16,000/month. If you’re in the 5–12M window that’s about $8k–$19.2k/month depending on where you land and whether you want a small committed discount.

If procurement needs a $25k+ PO threshold for net terms, we can discuss an initial card-billed pilot (up to $10k/mo) and transition to PO once contracts are complete.

Next steps I suggest: you share the rough monthly token range and procurement contact; I’ll send a short SOW + pricing attachment and loop in finance for simple PO exception if needed.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-sheet.pdf (1p)

—
Alex Martinez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com | (415) 555-0172

From: Elena Park <elena@orbitalcommerce.com>

Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: pilot pricing, monthly spend band & PO thresholds (Orbital Commerce)

Thanks, Alex — helpful summary. A few quick notes from my side after syncing with product and procurement: 

- Estimated pilot volume: roughly 5–12M tokens/month (this will vary by campaign spikes, but that’s our expected steady-state).
- Ballpark budget: our initial budget range for this pilot is $8k–$20k/month.
- Procurement constraints: our procurement team requires a PO for net-30 terms and prefers PO values >= $25k. For anything under that, they ask to route through our vendor-card process or our startup procurement partner (works only for vendors that can accept card billing).

Can your team support a short card-billed pilot (we'd put it on our corporate card) and then move to PO once the contract hits $25k+? If so, please send the SOW and pricing; I'll introduce you to procurement contact (procurement@orbitalcommerce.com) so they understand cadence/options.

Also a quick FYI: our product lead is particularly sensitive to latency at the 2–4 token step — we’ll want to validate a couple of live queries during the pilot.

—
Elena Park
Head of Product — Recommendations
Orbital Commerce
elena@orbitalcommerce.com
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@orbitalcommerce.com>, procurement@orbitalcommerce.com
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: pilot pricing, monthly spend band & PO thresholds (Orbital Commerce)

Elena — perfect, that helps a lot. Looping procurement here to get the vendor workflow and expected timeline.

Quick follow-up on the economics so procurement has clarity: below are two concrete options we commonly propose for a pilot that matches your 5–12M estimate. This is intentionally simple so your finance team can see monthly impact.

Option A — Card-billed pilot (no commit):
- Unit price: $2,400 / 1M tokens
- For 5–12M tokens -> $12k–$28.8k / month (billed to card)
- Good for fast validation, no contract required

Option B — Short commit (30-day commit with simple SOW):
- Commit: 10M tokens/month for 30 days
- Unit price: $1,600 / 1M tokens
- Monthly: ~$16k (predictable, eligible for invoice/PO after contract)

If procurement requires PO >= $25k for net-30, we can either: 1) run Option A on card while contract negotiations proceed, or 2) increase the commit band (e.g., 30M tokens/month at our mid-band pricing) to meet PO size if the product team is ready.

I attached a short SOW draft and the pricing sheet for procurement review. Can procurement confirm whether they can accept initial invoices < $25k on net-30 or if they require the $25k threshold to be enforced? If they do require $25k, Rafael and I can propose a one-time onboarding credit to bridge the first month so the PO hits threshold (subject to legal sign-off).

Attachments: SOW-draft-Orbital.docx, redwood-pricing-sheet.pdf

—
Alex Martinez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Park <elena@orbitalcommerce.com>, procurement@orbitalcommerce.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Approval request: pilot credit & PO exception for Orbital Commerce — summary + ask

Rafael / Grace — quick internal note and request for approval. Orbital (contact: Elena Park) is targeting a 5–12M tokens/month pilot. Procurement said they prefer PO >= $25k for net-30. Customer budget range is $8k–$20k/mo.

Options on table:
1) Card-billed pilot (no exception needed) — customer uses corporate card for up to $10k/mo; low friction.
2) Short commit 10M/mo at $1,600/1M (~$16k/mo) — would be invoice/PO eligible after SOW and contract.
3) If procurement enforces $25k PO minimum, we can: a) increase commit to 30M tokens/mo at mid-band pricing (~$30k/mo), or b) provide a one-time onboarding credit to push the first invoice to $25k so procurement can issue PO for net-30 (credit to be recovered over subsequent months).

My recommended path: approve a one-time onboarding credit up to $9k (to bring a 10M commit monthly invoice from ~$16k to $25k) contingent on legal approval and a 3-month review window. This preserves the lower commit level the product team prefers while satisfying procurement thresholds and getting contract signed.

Why I recommend this: keeps the pilot accessible to product, preserves a path to committed revenue, and avoids forcing an inflated commit that the team may not use.

Please reply with OK / needs changes by EOD — if you want, I can schedule a 15-min sync with legal to unblock wording.

Summary math (for quick reference):
- 10M tokens @ $1,600/1M = $16,000 -> need ~$9k credit to hit $25k PO threshold
- 30M tokens @ $1,000/1M = $30,000 -> meets PO without credit but requires a larger customer commitment

Thanks —
Alex
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
